name: No For An Answer
label: Revelation
lede: Orange County's straight edge band put out one six-song 7" on Revelation, lent its drum stool to a future Rage Against the Machine singer for a spell, and left Dan O'Mahony with a verdict he still delivers himself: the most musically feeble thing any of them did.

eras.title: Not called Just Say No
eras.text: Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby had already made noise together in Carry Nation. No For An Answer was the next try: songs from ex-Half Off bassist Jeff Boetto, and a message about more than just not drinking.

years.src: No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony · Wikipedia
years.h: Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby start [[Carry Nation|1440aef1-030f-4364-99d9-76eb61d9aa19]] in Orange County
years.p: Gavin Oglesby plays guitar. O'Mahony admits the chemistry was thin at first, and later calls the band arguably the most "gorilla" thing he ever did.

years.src: No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony · Wikipedia: No For An Answer
years.h: Just Say No nearly becomes the band's name
years.p: Bassist Jeff Boetto, ex-Half Off, arrives with songs, and the band forms in Orange County. O'Mahony decides "Just Say No was just not going to work."
years.xp:
The band takes its name from a song aimed at group identities and straight edge's own critics. Just Say No survived anyway, as the opening track of the first record.

The first line-up had Dan O'Mahony singing, Gavin Oglesby on guitar, Casey Jones on drums and John Mastropaulo on bass alongside Jeff Boetto, who was gone by the end of 1987.

O'Mahony also ran Workshed Records in the late 1980s. His description of the business model: the bands got 25 percent of the pressing, and no one made any money.

eras.title: Revelation goes west
eras.text: No For An Answer gave Revelation its first West Coast record. The drum stool, meanwhile, turned into a revolving door, and some famous names went through it.

years.h: You Laugh becomes Revelation's first West Coast record, REV 6
years.p: Six songs on a 7", from Just Say No to About Face. The first pressing ran in two batches a week apart, 972 and 1,031 copies, with identical white labels and the cover opening at the top.
years.xp:
The second pressing of 2,000 got silver labels and a cover that opened at the bottom. Some went to the band with no sleeves at all, 200 came in sleeves with an "I Spy" logo, and later copies used a live-photo sleeve.

When Revelation reissued it in 1997, the entire first pressing of the reissue had its labels on the wrong sides.

years.src: Wikipedia: No For An Answer · Wikipedia: Chris Bratton
years.h: Zack de la Rocha, future Rage Against the Machine singer, passes through on drums
years.p: Casey Jones and John Mastropaulo leave in 1988. Wikipedia lists [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]], later of [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], among the drummers who follow, before [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]] settles in.
years.xp: 1988 ran through de la Rocha, Quinn Mallard and Bratton on drums, with Sterling Wilson taking over bass and Rob Hayworth briefly on guitar. Bratton stayed into 1989 and went on to [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]] and [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]].

years.h: WABC-TV puts No For An Answer in its skinhead report
years.p: The 1988 news segment catches the band in the middle of a skinhead story. Dan O'Mahony rejects both the skinhead and straight edge labels and says the band is about more than not taking drugs.

eras.title: Hawker, CBGB and the flyers at the door
eras.text: Dan O'Mahony wanted the message in as many hands as possible, so the band left Revelation for Hawker, the Roadrunner offshoot. It got them a New York showcase and a flyer protest at the door, and then they were done.

years.src: No Echo: The Story of Hawker Records · No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony
yt: Live at F.O.E. Hall, Garden Grove, 1989
years.h: Hawker's first release, A Thought Crusade, cost about $5,000
years.p: Label owner John Bello says the money went on a record that isn't over-produced, and that Dan O'Mahony's voice reminded him of Sheer Terror and Killing Time. It is one of hardcore's first growls.
years.xp:
Bello singled out Domino Principle and Rusty Pipes. The songs took on drinking, drugs and child abuse. A woman named Peggy designed the cover from a photograph the band supplied, which they wanted in black and white.

O'Mahony explained the move from Revelation simply: if you had something to say, you had to get it to as many people as possible. Hawker, he says, had "twice the distribution that Rev had back then."

q: We all laughed about it. I think we even made fun of each other for it.
years.src: No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony · No Echo: The Story of Hawker Records
years.h: Flyers at the CBGB door say No For An Answer isn't hardcore
years.p: At Hawker's Free for All live-album showcase at CBGB, with [[Token Entry|535d0a8d-1f4c-4f0b-a384-b7d9fcadb7d3]], Wrecking Crew and Rest in Pieces, the [[Born Against|983825cd-4c25-45c5-adbb-3f9cdced6285]] and ABC No Rio crowd hands out the flyers.
years.xp:
Inside it was packed: John Bello puts the crowd at about 700 people in a 500-capacity room, the line stretched down the block, and No For An Answer borrowed gear from Wrecking Crew. The show became the Free for All live compilation.

O'Mahony took the protest as an argument, not a vendetta. The protesters, he says, didn't think he was evil, just wrong.

yt: Reseda, CA, Feb 4 1989, with Joe Foster
years.h: Joe Foster plays one show, and No For An Answer ends
years.p: Future [[Ignite|4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc]] and [[Speak 714|843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635]] guitarist Joe Foster fills in for a single show in 1989. The band stops that year, and Dan O'Mahony moves on to [[411|1d8b0619-dc78-4e25-b787-29ae6385c256]].
years.xp: 411's This Isn't Me arrives in 1991. A full set with Foster on guitar, from Reseda, California on February 4, 1989, is on YouTube.

eras.title: Back in print, labels backwards
eras.text: The band came back briefly in 1994, and the records came back with it: a CD pairing No For An Answer with Carry Nation, and a Revelation reissue of You Laugh with a pressing-plant mistake built in.

years.h: No For An Answer come back for 1994 and play Italy
years.p: Five years after splitting, Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby bring the band back for a short reunion. A full concert from Treviso, Italy survives on video.

years.src: Wikipedia: No For An Answer · Discogs
years.h: A Thought Crusade and Carry Nation's Face The Nation share a CD
years.p: Cargo and Tacklebox pair the two records, putting Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby's two '80s bands on one disc.

years.h: Revelation's You Laugh reissue comes back with the labels on backwards
years.p: Revelation re-presses the 7". All 1,000 copies of the reissue's first run have side A's label on side B.

eras.title: Only for a cause
eras.text: The original rhythm section came back, a new 7" followed on TKO, and No For An Answer took its place at Revelation's 25th birthday. Dan O'Mahony, by then a spoken-word performer, activist and author, set his own terms for playing at all.

years.cap: Dan O'Mahony reaches into the crowd, Revelation's 25th anniversary show, June 9, 2012
years.h: Casey Jones and John Mastropaulo rejoin No For An Answer
years.p: The 1987 rhythm section and Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby are a band again. The same year O'Mahony starts doing spoken word with [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] and [[Sam McPheeters|51e1e6b1-1498-4873-a3aa-351493cc7ee7]].

years.cap: Dan O'Mahony singing, Revelation's 25th anniversary show, June 9, 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: No For An Answer · Discogs: It Makes Me Sick
years.h: It Makes Me Sick is the first new music in 22 years
years.p: The reunited band releases the record on TKO Records, 22 years after A Thought Crusade.

years.cap: Dan O'Mahony with fans at the stage, Revelation's 25th anniversary show, June 10, 2012
years.h: No For An Answer play Revelation's 25th anniversary shows
years.p: Revelation celebrates 25 years with shows in California, and the band is on the bill. The Pomona set has Just Say No in it.
Revelation presses No For An Answer's 7" again: 548 copies on opaque yellow and 550 on opaque grey.

years.big: "The most musically feeble thing any of us did"
q: a much more important and challenging band than No For An Answer
years.src: No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony
years.h: Dan O'Mahony rates 411 above his first band
years.p: Looking back for No Echo, O'Mahony says No For An Answer was the weakest music any of them made but sincere in its message. He calls [[411|1d8b0619-dc78-4e25-b787-29ae6385c256]] the more important band.
years.xp:
O'Mahony was in straight edge from 1983 to 1990, seven years out of more than 35 in music, and says the obsession with it doesn't add up mathematically. No For An Answer hasn't played for pay in years; he won't do it without a cause behind the show.

Gavin Oglesby, who also played in [[Ignite|4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc]], went on to join O'Mahony in [[Done Dying|f17a4ac7-c333-4c13-8a23-886bc984a81e]], which O'Mahony says has "the most fun I've ever had in band."
